first.rationale: Simplifying onboarding directly addresses the current completion decline and has prior evidence of durable activation and faster time-to-value. This is better aligned with sustainable qualified revenue than promotional pricing, whose acquisition lift came with materially worse 30-day retention. Verification should focus on the two most directly relevant onboarding records before committing.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening and simplifying onboarding. The verified evidence directly addresses the 4% completion decline: shortened onboarding increased completion 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and improved 30-day retention 3%. Signup simplification also raised activation 9% and qualified revenue 4% in SMBs, though its slight retention decline and limited segment replication warrant guardrails and segment-level measurement. Promotional pricing is not preferred because prior evidence showed material retention harm despite acquisition lift.

final2.rationale: Switch this cycle’s single experiment to a narrowly targeted promotional-pricing test for price-sensitive SMB accounts showing competitive churn risk. The competitor’s deeper cut and doubled churn conversations make the immediate revenue threat more acute. Prior evidence supports acquisition and revenue lift in this exact segment, but the material 30-day retention decline rules out a broad rollout. Use strict eligibility, a limited cohort and duration, and retention, churn, margin, and qualified-revenue guardrails. Resume onboarding work in a later cycle.
